messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on svc-edge /v1/generate (global) — error_rate=18.7% over 1m, p95 latency=2.4s, spike started at 2026-03-14T13:02:36Z

alisha: paging oncall for svc-edge, I see a cascade of 502/504s from the gateway to runtime clusters. can someone grab this?

sre-oncall: I'm on it. acknowledging pager. grabbing logs and traffic graphs now.

ben: I can help — looks like retries increased traffic to older pool. seen similar with previous retry loops. are we hitting cb limits?

dmitri: putting live query: envoy stats show cluster.svc-runtime.upstream_rq_5xx: +12k in last 5m, upstream_rq_retry: +9k. route config recently changed this morning (new retry policy).

alisha: important — customers on Dedicated are seeing errors, some users reporting timeouts. customer-support, can you post a brief customer-impact note?

customer-support: posted to status page draft: "We are investigating elevated errors for parts of the API. Some requests may fail with 5xx or timeout. Engineers are investigating."

alisha: ok thanks. mitigation plan: 1) disable automatic retries at edge for /v1/generate, 2) increase circuit-breaker max connections for runtime cluster, 3) route traffic to canary-less pool. applying in that order to minimize cascading retries.

ben: agreed. I can flip the retry setting in edge envoy to 0. applying now.

ben: //config snippet
```
- name: retry_policy
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.router.filters.http.router.v3.RetryPolicy
    retry_on: "" # cleared to disable retries
    num_retries: 0
```

ben: patched envoy via config manager (canary=0): POST /admin/v1/route/patch -> 200. watching metrics.

sre-oncall: after disabling retries, upstream_rq_retry dropped to near 0 in 30s, 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 7% and trending. p95 latency trending down. good signal.

dmitri: still seeing some 502s from a subset of runtime pods (runtime-pool-2). looks like they are getting overloaded — CBs tripping then failing open to cluster leading to 5xx. checking circuit breaker config.

alisha: let's temporarily increase max_pending_requests and max_connections for that cluster to stop immediate tripping while we roll a fix. we can revert after.

ben: bumping cb thresholds now in runtime cluster config:
```
circuit_breakers:
- priority: DEFAULT
  thresholds:
  - max_connections: 20000
    max_pending_requests: 10000
    max_requests: 100000
    max_retries: 3
```

ben: applied and pushed config. new config diff rolled to all active proxies.

sre-oncall: after cb bump, errors dropped to 3.2% and latency p95 ~1.1s. runtime-pool-2 CPU spike settled. looks stable for now.

alisha: good. next steps: 1) rollback the morning retry policy change that enabled cross-cluster retries (that introduced amplification), 2) investigate why runtime-pool-2 had degraded capacity (OOM? GC?), 3) schedule a postmortem.

dmitri: grabbing pod logs for runtime-pool-2 - seeing spikes of GC pause and a few OOMKills around 12:55Z correlating with traffic surge. pointing to memory pressure under retry amplification.

customer-support: updated public status: "We have reduced impact; service is recovering. Some requests may still see errors while we complete mitigations."

alisha: handing off to ben for follow-up (config rollback + postmortem). I'm going offline in 10m but will be reachable. ben, can you own the write-up and include playbook changes to disallow cross-cluster retries by default?

ben: will do. immediate follow-up actions I'm taking now:
- revert the retry policy change from this morning (git rev 1a2b3c -> deploy)
- add a guard in runtime autoscaler to avoid undersized pool sizes during spikes
- create a monitoring alert for retry amplification (retry_count / total_requests > 0.05)

sre-oncall: tagging incident record: INC-2026-0314-1, severity P2. Adding timeline and mitigation notes.

dmitri: saving logs and perf profiles to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026-0314-1/

alisha: quick note for postmortem — list of hypotheses: retry policy change + low CB thresholds + runtime memory regression. we'll validate.

customer-support: notifying affected Dedicated customers via email template A with current status and expected next update in 2h.

ben: done with rollback PR and starting a rolling deploy to remove the retry-on-cross-cluster flag. taking it slow (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%).

ben: at 20% traffic now, metrics stable. no error spike. proceeding to 100%.

sre-oncall: closing active paging loop — oncall remains assigned for follow-up. please update the incident record when complete.

alisha: thanks team. final summary for handoff: root cause preliminary = retry amplification after an overly permissive retry policy + circuit-breaker thresholds too low on runtime cluster + memory pressure on pool-2. Mitigations = disabled edge retries, bumped CBs, rolled back policy. Next: postmortem, autoscaler guard, monitoring alert, and customer follow-ups.

ben: I'll file the postmortem draft and assign owners. tagging for follow-up: @alisha @dmitri @sre-oncall.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0314-1 created. Severity: P2. Playbook link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0314-1

sre-oncall: thanks all.
